data.one_liner: Check and request notification permissions on iOS and Android.
data.what_it_does: Provides static methods to query the current notification permission status and to request permission from the user. Handles platform‑specific behaviours such as provisional status on iOS and opening app settings on denial.
use_when: You need to know if the user has allowed notifications before scheduling them
You want to prompt the user for notification permission at a custom point in the app flow
You need a lightweight way to manage only the permission aspect without a full notification library
avoid_when: You already use a full‑featured notification package that includes its own permission handling
You need advanced push‑notification features like remote messaging or background handling
strengths: Simple, small API focused on permissions
Supports iOS provisional status and Android settings redirection
Null‑safe and works with the latest Android embedding
weaknesses: Only manages permissions, not actual notification display
Requires manual Podfile edit for Objective‑C projects
No built‑in handling for remote push tokens
data.setup_notes: Add use_frameworks! to the iOS Podfile for Objective‑C projects; on Android the plugin opens app settings when denied; no additional Gradle changes required.
